name: Tina Maze

name: Nina Simone

evidence_summary: Nina Simone, born Eunice Kathleen Waymon, began playing piano at age 3 in Tryon, North Carolina, and was playing in church by age 6. Her classical piano training was funded by local white benefactors who established a special fund for her education. She attended the Allen High School for Girls as valedictorian and studied at Juilliard before being rejected by the Curtis Institute, which she attributed to racism. She began performing in Atlantic City clubs in 1954 and recorded her debut album in December 1957 at age 24.
starting_point: Born Eunice Kathleen Waymon in Tryon, North Carolina to a Methodist preacher mother and a father who worked as an entertainer, barber, and dry-cleaner; sixth of eight children in a modest African American family.
current_position: Died on April 21, 2003 at age 70 in Carry-le-Rouet, France; final status: legendary singer and civil rights activist known as the 'High Priestess of Soul.'

Died on April 21, 2003 in Carry-le-Rouet, France.

evidence_summary: Toller Cranston began skating at age 7 in Hamilton, Ontario, after his parents bought him hockey skates. After struggling at the senior level and failing to make the 1968 Olympic team, he began working with Ellen Burka in Toronto, leading to his first Canadian senior title in 1971 at age 22.
